entries.proposition: Design: two successive ABA n-of-1 trials, intrathecal magnesium then ketamine, designed from the patient's in vitro findings.
entries.snippet: Two successive ABA (A = no treatment epoch; B = treatment epoch) n-of-1 treatment trials, using intrathecal magnesium and then ketamine, were designed and implemented based on our in vitro findings.

entries.proposition: Treatment was not randomised because of the invasive intervention.
entries.snippet: Treatment was not randomized given the invasive nature of the intervention.

entries.proposition: The magnesium trial was ended early because of hypotension.
entries.snippet: due to hypotension which responded to intervention.

entries.proposition: Result: marked fall in spike density and amplitude and rise in EEG complexity, with a clinical improvement in wakefulness and interaction (video).
entries.snippet: Intrathecal MgSO4 administration led to a marked reduction in spike density and amplitude (Figure 1 C&D) and increase in EEG complexity (Figure 1 E), correlating with a clinical improvement in wakefulness and interaction

entries.proposition: Clinical seizures fell from 13 to 8 over 24 hours pre and post.
entries.snippet: Clinical EEG indicated a reduction in seizures (tonic or behavioral arrest) from 13 to 8 (24 h pre-/post-treatment).

entries.proposition: In vitro: the variant reduced sensitivity to magnesium inhibition about seven-fold.
entries.snippet: A 7 fold reduction in the inhibition sensitivity to endogenous inhibitor Mg++ (based on IC50 potency) was evident.

entries.proposition: The authors claim level 2 evidence for short-term benefit.
entries.snippet: provides level 2 evidence (Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine) supporting a short-term benefit of IT MgSO4.

entries.proposition: Authors: limitations are non-randomised, unblinded and short-term; they argue automatic quantitative neurophysiology reduces observer bias.
entries.snippet: Limitations of our study included the non-randomized, unblinded, and short-term nature of our trial.

entries.proposition: Authors: it is unclear whether the neurophysiological benefit would translate into clinical improvements of value to the family.
entries.snippet: it is unclear whether this would translate into clinical improvements of value to the family, such as improved wakefulness, enhanced interaction or developmental milestone attainment.

entries.proposition: Authors: the rapid clearance of CSF magnesium leaves sustained benefit unproven.
entries.snippet: Given the rapid clearance of CSF Mg++, it is also unclear if the short-term benefits (neurophysiology and seizure-control) we observed could be sustained over the long run

entries.proposition: Outpatient oral ketamine was followed by more than 30 seizure-free days, uncontrolled and unmeasured against a baseline.
entries.snippet: This regimen led to complete seizure-freedom for more than 30 days, with periods of improved wakefulness and diminished irritability, although the patient continued to experience intermittent dystonic spasms.

entries.proposition: The child died more than a year after the trial of respiratory insufficiency after a rhinovirus infection, judged unrelated.
entries.snippet: Unfortunately, he passed away due to respiratory insufficiency after contacting rhinovirus more than one year after his n-of-1 treatment trial.

entries.proposition: An earlier mechanism-matched drug (memantine) was stopped after 5 days because seizures rose.
entries.snippet: memantine was trialed at age one year but was trialed for only 5 days as seizure burden rose at the time of initiation and the family self-discontinued the medication.

entries.proposition: Oral or intravenous magnesium was considered futile because of poor brain penetration.
entries.snippet: Oral and intravenous magnesium were discussed, but considered futile given published data indicating poor blood-brain barrier penetration

entries.proposition: Supplement: the hospital review board deemed the intervention off-label treatment, not research.
entries.snippet: The patient’s parents provided their consent to participate in this trial, although it was deemed “not research” (but rather off-label treatment) by the Phoenix Children’s Hospital IRB.

entries.proposition: Supplement: the evidence level is stated as level 2, downgraded slightly because the intervention was not blinded.
entries.snippet: This study was considered level 2 evidence based on Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine 2011 Levels of Evidence guidelines, downgraded slightly because the intervention in question was not blinded.

entries.proposition: Supplement: pre and post values over time-matched epochs were compared by paired t-tests assuming unequal variances.
entries.snippet: Pre- and post-treatment mean values and fold change were further compared using paired t-tests assuming unequal variances, with significance set at p<0.05.

entries.proposition: Fig 1C-E: spike events fell from about 280 to under 20 after the lowest dose and stayed low; amplitude fell from 10.4 to 4 and rose with dose; complexity jumped from 3.2 to 6.1 and fell with dose; at the two washout epochs CSF magnesium was still 91 and 67 against 26 at baseline and values stayed away from baseline.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 1C spike events baseline about 280 (458 epochs) then about 4, 12, 20, 5, 4, 4, 3 over the dose steps and two washout epochs with CSF Mg 26, 42, 57, 105, 260, 298, 91 and 67; stars on all treatment and washout epochs; Fig 1D amplitude about 10.4 at baseline, 4.1 at the first dose, rising to about 6.1 at the last dose, 6.6 and 6.1 in the washout epochs; Fig 1E complexity about 3.2 at baseline, 6.15 at the first dose, falling to about 4.3 and 4.5 in the washout epochs. Fig 1A in vitro table: magnesium IC50 21.3 for wild type and 154.2 for the variant, 7.2-fold effect; glutamate, glycine, proton and zinc parameters no effect.
